links.outcome: Privacy leakage and clinical utility of LLMs with vs without privacy-preserving methods
links.effect: Unprotected Med42-v2-8B: utility 3.87/5, leakage 72.8%. Supervised fine-tuning: utility 4.25, leakage 38.9%. Local differential privacy: leakage 20.5%, utility 3.03.
links.quote: Relative to unprotected Med42-v2-8B (utility 3.87/5; leakage 72.8%), supervised fine-tuning improved utility to 4.25 and reduced leakage to 38.9%, whereas local differential privacy reduced leakage to 20.5% but lowered utility to 3.03.

unlisted_practices: Benchmarking privacy-utility trade-off of retrieval-augmented LLMs using contextual-leakage evaluation
Automated NLI-based evaluator for detecting privacy leakage in LLM outputs

screen.practice: privacy-preserving methods (differential privacy and fine-tuning guardrails against contextual leakage)
screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating LLM clinical utility alongside privacy leakage risks and testing privacy-preserving mitigation techniques.
